label: copy-phase input v (re-fed copied token v), from 2nd copied token on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is v, i.e. the model has just emitted v and it is fed back (in_tok v, never a first occurrence). Never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, nor on any other input token. When v is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, input = orig(0)) it fires rarely and weakly; activation rises with copy position: v at copy position 1 gives ~0.5 of max, at position 3+ ~0.85-1.0. Output token and neighbouring tokens barely modulate it. Dev: P=1.00, R=0.96, F1=0.98, mass recall 0.998.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split the predicate has precision 1.00, recall 0.961, F1 0.980 and mass recall 0.998. There are 0 false positives.

All 3020 missed test activations are the first copied token when it is v (recall_idx 1, input = orig(0)). They are weak (about 0.02-0.07 of max) and hold 0.2% of the activation mass. The explanation already describes them. Adding recall_idx==1 alone scores precision 0.18 and recall 0.039, so dropping the recall_idx condition makes F1 worse (test F1 0.918, precision 0.848).

Profile claims check out. Activation is zero in the original phase and at the delimiter, and every bit of activation mass falls on in_tok v. out_tok, prev_tok and next_out are flat (lift about 1.0-2.1x, spread evenly). Magnitude grows with copy position: a v at orig index 1 (recall_idx 2) is about 0.47-0.51 of max, and later positions reach 0.8-1.0, matching the '0.5 then 0.85-1.0' claim. The wording 'copy position 1' is ambiguous: it means orig index 1, not recall_idx 1.
The label states the same thing as the predicate and does not overclaim.
